pr_title: fix: Fix lazy schema for `group_by_dynamic` and `rolling`
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/11339

#### Changes

* Fixes the ordering of columns in the schema - aggregation columns should be at the end.
* Properly inserts `_lower_bound` and `_upper_bound` into the schema when `include_boundaries` is specified for `group_by_dynamic` _(Should these columns have better names?_ 🤔 
* Refactor some related tests

issue_context.title: Lazy schema for `group_by_dynamic` is incorrect
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

Here is a reproducible example (Note the `include_boundaries=True`):
```python
from datetime import datetime
import polars as pl

lf = pl.LazyFrame(
    {
        "time": pl.datetime_range(
            start=datetime(2021, 12, 16),
            end=datetime(2021, 12, 16, 3),
            interval="30m",
            eager=True,
        ),
        "n": range(7),
    }
)
lf_uncollected_gpd = lf.group_by_dynamic(
    "time", every="1h", closed="right", include_boundaries=True
).agg(
    [
        pl.col("time").min().alias("time_min"),
        pl.col("time").max().alias("time_max"),
    ]
)
```
The below line succeeds:
```python
print(lf_uncollected_gpd.collect().with_columns(x=pl.col("_upper_boundary").dt.time()))
```
but the below line fails:
```python
print(lf_uncollected_gpd.with_columns(x=pl.col("_upper_boundary").dt.time()).collect())
```

### Log output

```shell

  File "/some/path/test_polars_operations.py", line 28, in test_lazy_boundary_with_columns

    return function(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/python/package/path/lib/python3.9/site-packages/polars/lazyframe/frame.py", line 1703, in collect
    return wrap_df(ldf.collect())
exceptions.ColumnNotFoundError: _upper_boundary

Error originated just after this operation:
AGGREGATE
	[col("time").min().alias("time_min"), col("time").max().alias("time_max")] BY [] FROM
  DF ["time", "n"]; PROJECT */2 COLUMNS; SELECTION: "None"
```


### Issue description

When using lazy frame, it seems like its not possible to operate on the `_upper_boundary`/`_lower_boundary` columns generated by `group_by_dynamic`. 

### Expected behavior

Operations on the boundary columns succeed

review_comments: Not entirely sure, but I believe we must insert those at the start of the schema?

First are the "keys" (specified in the `by` parameter), then are the `_lower_bound`/`_upper_bound` columns if specified, then the index column, and then the aggregation columns.

This is the way it's currently implemented, I am just making the schema fit to what actually happens. I have to admit I was scratching my head a little bit about this ordering myself...

What would make sense to me is:

* Index column (e.g. `index`)
* Bounds if `include_bounds=True`, named after the index column (e.g. `index_lower_bound`, `index_upper_bound`)
* Additional groups if `by` is specified (e.g. `group1`, `group2`, ...)
* Aggregations (e.g. `agg1`, `agg2`, ...).

So if all are present you get `[index, index_lower_bound, index_upper_bound, group1, group2, ..., agg1, agg2, ...]`

Status quo gives you: `[group1, group2, ..., index_lower_bound, index_upper_bound, index, agg1, agg2, ...]`
_(See [docs](https://pola-rs.github.io/polars/docs/python/dev/reference/lazyframe/api/polars.LazyFrame.group_by_dynamic.html#polars.LazyFrame.group_by_dynamic) for data example)_

If that sounds more sensible than the status quo, now is the time to change it 😄 I can do that in a separate PR, this fix is valid regardless.
I mean more. Do we return the same ordering as the materialization? That's what is important. I didn't want to break. :smile:
We do! That's the whole point of this PR 😄  There are tests for that. So this is safe to merge.
